newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo NBY to launch dinar interbank mkt, repo deals.
newsitem.headline: Yugo NBY to launch dinar interbank mkt, repo deals.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) will expand its open market operations by institutionalising the dinar interbank market and introducing repo deals, NBY Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic said on Tuesday.
Yugoslavia has had no money market for several years, ever since its official money market Trziste Novca transformed into a brokerage house.

"We shall have to formalise the money market and with the payment system reverting to banks we must find a model for the money market to work night and day, to enable that money is lent and borrowed and that all payments are cleared at the end of the day," Banovic told Reuters.

The move is aimed to secure liquidity for the banking sector once all payment operations returned to banks, Banovic told an annual shareholders meeting of the Yugoslav largest brokerage house Trziste Novca.
Currently payment operations are conducted, cleared and controlled by the state Payment Operations Office.

"The key is to provide sufficient liquidity for the entire system. In future, NBY will become a distributor of liquidity for the banking sector, it will conduct some kind of recycling of surplus liquidity, taking it from those who have and giving it to those who need," Banovic said.

The central bank said this would increase its role on the financial market. The NBY's market activity has been limited to selling its short-term bonds to regulate liquidity of banks. Although the NBY says its operations are monetary neutral, it has rarely added liquidity by buying securities from banks.

Banovic said the central bank will soon announce a new model of maintaining liquidity of the national payment system, in which it will be possible to cash in securities to bridge temporary liquidity problems.
He also insisted the new system will not lead to any increase in the money supply.

Banovic said NBY will launch repo deals for longer-dated securities. "We expect some longer-dated securities to appear on the market soon, and in that case why not develop repo deals." Currently, the Yugoslav financial market trades mainly in paper maturing in 10-15 days.

Apart from creating an environment in which it will be able to perform open market operations, the NBY planned to step up control of banks, help them clear problem-ridden segments and prepare for coming to the money market.

"This will lead to a more rational operation of banks. It will influence interest rates and alongside we hope that banks will build trust among themselves and start trading surplus liquidity on the new institutionalised market," Banovic said.

Once the official money market is there, the central bank said it would be able to influence money rates with its discount rate policy, Banovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
